questions.q: Log files are written daily, accessed often for a week, rarely after, and must be instantly retrievable for compliance. Best storage strategy?
options: Lifecycle: Standard -> Std-IA after 30 days -> Glacier IR after 90
questions.explanation: Lifecycle matches access pattern; Glacier IR keeps instant retrieval for rarely-touched compliance data at low cost. Deep Archive has hours-long retrieval; Std-IA before 30 days incurs minimum-charge penalties.

questions.q: A batch image-processing job runs nights and weekends, is fault-tolerant, and can resume partial work. Cheapest compute?
questions.explanation: Spot gives up to 90% off for interruption-tolerant batch work. RIs are for steady-state; On-Demand is the most expensive option here.

questions.q: An API gets traffic 5 minutes per hour, ~zero otherwise, and each burst completes in under 5 seconds. Cheapest architecture?
questions.explanation: Lambda bills per 1ms of execution - near-zero cost for 5-min/hour bursts, no idle servers. Always-on EC2 pays 24/7.

questions.q: A dev database is used ~2 hours per day by engineers with unpredictable load. Cheapest managed relational option?
questions.explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 (or v1 for dev) scales to near-zero between use; pay-per-use fits 2hr/day unpredictable load. Always-on RDS bills 24/7. DynamoDB isn't relational.
